newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- slight gains near close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- slight gains near close.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices edged slightly higher in late Monday trading, but market participants said the improved tone was almost entirely on quotes with few bonds actually changing hands.
Traders had expected a quiet session, with most participants sidelined until the Federal Open Market Committee meeting Tuesday.
The FOMC is widely expected to bring a 25-basis-point tightening in short-term rates, and such a move has been factored into most of the yield curve, analysts said.
One municipal analyst pegged the cash market overall at unchanged to up 1/8 point on the day. The analyst also noted about $100 million of bid-wanted lists that circulated during the day.
The government long bond, meanwhile, was up 19/32 at 96-10/32 to yield 6.92 percent.

Among actively traded municipal secondary market issues, bids on Dade County, Fla., FGIC water and sewer 5-1/4s of 2026 were unchanged at 5.79 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were up one basis point from Friday at 5.80 percent.

In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed up 3/32 at 113-10/32, while the June T-bond contract was up at 8/32 at 108-31/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 139 ticks from 144 at the close on Friday.
In addition to the much anticipated FOMC meeting, traders said they are also closely watching the two-year and five-year auctions on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The government is scheduled to sell $17.25 billion of two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday.
Municipal bond sales for Tuesday are expected to total $280 million in 26 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $106 million in six sales, with a $44 million Delaware State Housing deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the the list.
On the competitive side, 20 sales totaling $175 million are on the schedule, a $39 million Connecticut Health and Educational deal at 1100 EST is the largest.
